THE SQUARE GATEHOUSE AND THE COPPER BELL: a great square gatehouse of warm honey-coloured stone in uneven flat-banded courses, each face stepping into shadow through three flat dithered bands, the wide arch cut off-centre through its base and the whole mass turned three-quarters to the camera, the long wall of the same honey stone running out of frame past both flanks, the ground a wide band of wet cobbles crossing the bottom of the frame, window boxes crammed with orange and yellow flowers at uneven heights up the stone face, and one great bronze bell hung in the arch on a heavy timber yoke with a green rope trailing down from its clapper

THE DRUM TOWER AND THE GREAT WHEEL: one fat round drum tower of pale grey stone in chunky stacked courses standing off to one side of the picture with the archway cut through its foot and a steep conical roof of deep blue tiles on top, a second smaller drum well off to the left and plainly shorter, the wall crossing the whole picture and running out of frame both ways, three long strips of cloth in scarlet, saffron and jade twisting edge-on in the wind from poles on the taller drum, and the enormous timber wheel and rope that lifts the heavy iron lattice gate mounted out in plain view on the stone face above the arch

THE TIMBER GATE-HOUSE AND THE PLUM TREE: a tall timber-framed gate-house painted deep brick red and pale cream standing over the arch, its upper two floors leaning out above the near ground on carved beam-ends, the stone wall running out of frame from each flank in flat stepped bands of dark grey, the ground a wide band of trodden earth and old straw across the bottom of the frame, ivy climbing one whole side of the timber frame to the roofline, and a crooked tree grown straight out of a crack forty feet up the stone beside the gate its roots splayed flat across the stone in dark stepped lines

THE LONG LOW RANGE AND THE STONE FISH: a long low gate-range of pale sandstone and dark timber with the arch sitting at the right-hand end of it, the whole range crossing the picture from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame on both sides, its roofline stepping up and down in three uneven jumps, the ground a wide band of damp sand across the bottom, a wooden stair zigzagging up the outside of the range in chunky stepped pixel edges, and a carved stone fish jutting from the wall above the arch with its mouth open wide and a bright thread of rainwater spitting from it into a stone trough below

THE CLIFF GATE AND THE BEEHIVE: the archway and its square gatehouse built straight into the foot of a great pale rock face, the wall of rough-cut stone running along the cliff's base and out of frame on both sides, the gatehouse mass turned three-quarters with one flank vanishing into the rock, the ground a wide band of pale grit and loose stones crossing the bottom of the frame, hanging bundles of drying herbs and onions on iron hooks beside the arch, and a straw beehive of golden colour tucked deep into a niche cut into the stone to the left of the arch with a faint smear of old honey darkening the stone below it

THE WATER GATE AND THE ROPE HOIST: a gatehouse of dark greenish stone standing on four broad square stone piers set in shallow water, the arch opening straight onto the water below, the wall running out of frame on both sides across the picture, the gatehouse mass turned three-quarters so one pier recedes, a stone bridge of three uneven arches crossing the water and running out of the left edge of the frame, and a rope-and-basket hoist running from an upper window of the gatehouse down to a small timber platform beside the nearest pier with a pile of small round cheeses sitting in the basket

THE TWIN-ARCHED MASS AND THE BOOT-SCRAPER: a wide gatehouse of dark red stone with two arches side by side, the left one open with its heavy iron lattice gate half-raised and stopped, the right one long since bricked up in paler stone and covered with a lopsided sheet of ivy, the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting off to the right of the picture, the wall crossing from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame on both sides, the ground a wide band of worn cobbles across the bottom, and a boot-scraper set into the stone at the base of the open arch worn into a deep groove by what looks like a century of boots

THE STEPPED STONE GATE AND THE DOVECOTE: a mass of warm amber stone stepping back in three uneven stages above the arch, each stage a wide flat walkway with a low parapet of square stone teeth along its edge, the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting off to the left, the wall crossing the picture and running out of frame both ways in chunky stepped pixel courses, the ground a wide band of pale grass across the bottom of the frame, and a whole dovecote of white-painted timber built onto the side of the lowest stage with thirty small round holes in its face and a wooden perch rail below them

THE SQUARE GATEHOUSE AND THE TILTED CHIMNEY: a great square gatehouse of dark charcoal-grey stone in flat dithered bands stepping into shadow on the near face, its steep tiled roof of mossy green pulled low over the top like a hat, the arch cut off-centre and the whole mass turned three-quarters to the camera, the long wall running out of frame past both flanks, the ground a wide band of wet cobblestones crossing the bottom of the frame, firewood stacked to shoulder height against the left flank with a striped pot sitting on top, and a chimney rising from one side of the roof with its own tiny tiled hat sitting slightly crooked on its top

THE DRUM TOWER AND THE STONE OWL: one fat round drum tower of deep rust-red stone in blocky stacked courses with a wide tiled roof pulled low and the archway cut through the drum's foot, a second much smaller drum standing well off to the right at barely half the height, the wall crossing the picture from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame both ways, window boxes of deep purple flowers at three uneven heights on the flat walls between the drums, and a carved stone owl's head the size of a barrel jutting straight out of the wall well to one side of the arch, lichen in pale patches across its brow

THE TIMBER GATE-HOUSE AND THE KETTLE: a tall timber-framed gate-house painted deep green and warm yellow standing over the arch, its top floor leaning out on carved bracket beam-ends above the near ground, the stone wall running out of frame from each flank in flat grey courses, the ground a wide band of trodden earth crossing the bottom, three long strips of cloth in deep blue, white and copper-orange twisting edge-on from poles on each side of the upper floor, and a small brazier burning amber in a niche beside the arch with a fat black kettle sitting beside it on the stone

THE CLIFF GATE AND THE WATER SPOUT: the arch and its square gatehouse of pale cream stone built straight into the base of a towering dark rock face, the wall of the same pale stone running along the cliff's base and out of frame on both sides, the gatehouse turned three-quarters with one flank pressed into the rock, the ground a wide band of wet gravel crossing the bottom of the frame, a wooden stair zigzagging up the gate face in chunky stepped pixel edges to a walkway along the top, and a spout high on the stone face pouring a bright thin thread of rainwater down the wall into a wide stone trough at ground level

THE LONG LOW RANGE AND THE HANGING PANS: a long low gate-range of warm golden sandstone and dark oak timber with the arch at the left end of it, the range crossing the whole picture from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame on both sides, its roofline uneven with the arch end tallest and two lower sections stepping down to the right, the ground a wide band of dry golden grit across the bottom of the frame, ivy climbing the right half of the range in one lopsided green sheet, and a row of copper pans hung on iron hooks beside the small low door cut into the big timber door of the arch with warm light spilling from that small door

THE WATER GATE AND THE STONE BEAR: a gatehouse of pale yellow stone on three uneven stone piers set in still dark water, the arch opening onto the water's surface, the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting off to the right of the picture, the wall crossing from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame both ways, a stone bridge of two uneven spans crossing the water and running out of the right edge of the frame, and a carved stone bear's head as broad as a cart wheel jutting straight out of the wall well to one side of the arch, its muzzle worn smooth and pale from years of luck-rubbing by passing travellers

THE TWIN-ARCHED MASS AND THE BRONZE BELL: a wide gatehouse of warm pale stone in flat-banded courses with two arches side by side, the right arch open with the two great timber doors standing wide flat against the wall, the left arch bricked up in darker stone and used as a lean-to with a small low timber roof against it, the whole mass turned three-quarters and off to the left, the wall running out of frame on both sides, the ground a wide band of old cobbles crossing the bottom, and one great bronze bell hung on a heavy timber yoke in the open arch with a long knotted rope trailing down from it to the ground

THE SQUARE GATEHOUSE AND THE IVY LION: a great square gatehouse of deep red sandstone in blocky uneven courses, each face stepping into shadow through two flat dithered bands, the arch cut through its base off to the right and the whole mass turned three-quarters to the camera, the long wall running out of frame past both flanks, the ground a wide band of worn cobblestones crossing the bottom of the frame, ivy gone right up one whole flank in a lopsided green sheet to the row of square stone teeth along the top, and a fat carved stone lion's head jutting right out above the arch with real moss packed thick in its open mouth

THE STEPPED STONE GATE AND THE SHRINE: a mass of pale buff stone stepping back in three uneven stages above the arch, each stage a broad walkway with a low parapet of square stone teeth along its edge, the first stage widest and the top stage narrowest and set well to one side, the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting off to the right, the wall crossing the picture and running out of frame both ways in flat stepped courses, the ground a wide band of short pale grass crossing the bottom, and a small stone shrine cut into the wall to the right of the arch with a shallow bowl of bright yellow and red flowers set into it

THE DRUM TOWER AND THE WOODEN STAIR: one fat round drum tower of warm amber stone with the archway cut through its foot and a steep conical roof of dark orange tiles on top, a second drum well off to the left and clearly a full floor shorter with a flat parapet on top instead of a cone, the wall crossing the picture from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame both ways, five round paper lanterns strung along under the arch with two of them still dark, and a wooden stair of uneven zigzagging flights built against the outside of the taller drum in chunky stepped pixel edges running from the near ground to the walkway at the top

THE TIMBER GATE-HOUSE AND THE SHRINE FLOWERS: a tall timber-framed gate-house painted deep blue and warm cream standing over the arch, its upper floor and attic leaning out over the near ground on carved beam-ends, the stone wall running out of frame from each flank in chunky grey courses, the ground a wide band of wet cobbles crossing the bottom of the frame, a rope-and-basket hoist running from one upper window of the gate-house down to the near ground with a bundle of dark green onions in the basket, and a small stone shrine set into the wall to the right of the arch with a shallow bowl of pink and white flowers sitting in it

THE CLIFF GATE AND THE TILTED TREE: the arch and a short square gatehouse of pale grey stone built straight into the base of a vast dark rock face, the wall running along the cliff's base and out of frame on both sides in flat stepped courses, the gatehouse turned three-quarters with its right flank merging into the cliff stone, the ground a wide band of loose pale grit crossing the bottom of the frame, nets and baskets on iron hooks along the wall to the left of the arch, and a whole tree grown at a steep angle straight out of a crack in the rock face above the gatehouse with its roots gripping three courses of stone

THE WATER GATE AND THE LANTERNS: a gatehouse of warm dark brown stone on five uneven stone piers in shallow green water, the arch sitting off-centre through the gatehouse base and opening onto the water, the whole mass turned three-quarters and off to the left of the picture, the wall running out of frame on both sides, a stone bridge of three uneven arches crossing the water and running out of the left edge of the frame, a row of seven round paper lanterns strung along under the arch with three of them still dark and one swinging slightly out of line, and a heavy iron lattice gate with its portcullis bars half-raised and stopped inside the arch

THE TWIN-ARCHED MASS AND THE WHEEL: a wide gatehouse of pale greenish stone in uneven flat-banded courses with two arches side by side, the left arch open with a heavy iron lattice gate half-raised and stopped, the right arch bricked up in warmer stone and covered with a thick lopsided sheet of ivy from ground to parapet, the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting to the right of the picture, the wall crossing from the left edge to the right edge and running out of frame both ways, the ground a wide band of wet cobbles crossing the bottom, and the enormous timber wheel and rope that lifts the iron lattice gate sitting out in plain view on the stone face above the open arch

THE LONG LOW RANGE AND THE STONE TROUGH: a long low gate-range of warm honey stone and dark painted timber with the arch near the right end, the range crossing the whole picture from the left edge to the right edge and running well out of frame on both sides, its roofline stepping in three uneven jumps from low at the left to tall at the arch end, the ground a wide band of damp earth and old grass crossing the bottom of the frame, window boxes of deep red flowers at uneven heights on the stone faces, and a stone spout high on the wall above the arch pouring a bright thread of rainwater down the stone face into a wide stone trough at the base of the wall

THE SQUARE GATEHOUSE AND THE HOIST: a great square gatehouse of pale blue-grey stone in uneven flat-banded courses with hard pixel steps on every edge, the arch cut off-centre through its base and the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting to the left of the picture, the long wall running out of frame past both flanks, the ground a wide band of pale cobblestones crossing the bottom of the frame, snow heaped on every ledge and icicles hanging in a row of uneven lengths below the parapet of square stone teeth along the top, and a rope-and-basket hoist running from an upper window of the gatehouse down to the near ground with a fat round loaf sitting in the basket

THE STEPPED STONE GATE AND THE CROW TREE: a mass of warm red stone stepping back in three uneven stages above the arch, each stage a broad walkway with a low parapet of square stone teeth of uneven heights, the lowest stage widest and plainly older than the two above it, the whole mass turned three-quarters and sitting off to the left of the picture, the wall crossing the picture and running out of frame both ways in chunky stacked courses, the ground a wide band of trodden earth crossing the bottom, and a whole crooked tree growing out of a deep crack in the stone face between the first and second stages with its roots splayed across the stone in flat dark stepped lines
